is: Seven agent definitions: six briefs for the instances zaf launches (team, programmer, keeper, planning, challenger, release) and `designer`, the judgment lane of the Engineer's design session.
conventions: each file is `<role>.md`: frontmatter (name, description, model, effort, turns, tool limits, color), then a one-page brief: purpose, input, output, lifecycle, budget, never-list, verbs in order

the six zaf role briefs begin, right after the frontmatter, with the exact bytes of zaf's interface page so every instance shares a cached prompt prefix; when the page changes it is pasted into all six (the pack README's cmp loop checks this)
tool limits live in frontmatter: keeper gets Read/Grep/Glob only; team, planning, challenger and release cannot edit files; programmer cannot spawn agents; designer is unrestricted

fs.name: challenger.md
fs.role: comments on each planned task that is not exact, before the Engineer signs the epic (opus, xhigh)

fs.name: designer.md
fs.role: design-session judgment lane: architect's package, fresh challenge of signed documents, one-way-door review; no interface prefix

fs.name: keeper.md
fs.role: answers one `zaf ask` from the design pages with verbatim quotes, or says not settled (haiku, 10 turns)

fs.name: planning.md
fs.role: turns a signed epic into exact Task and Spike sub-issues, or re-plans after a ruling (opus, xhigh)

fs.name: programmer.md
fs.role: one task, one round, green in its own workspace from the task's zaf brief pack (sonnet, high, 60 turns)

fs.name: release.md
fs.role: closes a milestone: checks musts, gathers release reviews and a retrospective, then files tasks or merges and tags (opus, xhigh)

fs.name: team.md
fs.role: team instance: builds a batch of one epic's ready tasks, a programmer per task, merges into the integration branch (opus, xhigh, 200 turns)

notes: in this repo the interface page is `zaf/assets/interface.md`; all six briefs matched it byte for byte on 2026-11-03
frontmatter model and effort are the by-hand defaults; the spawner passes ZAF.toml's `[roles.<role>]` model, effort, turns and profile instead
keeper.md points to zaf's own keeper prompt (`zaf/assets/keeper.md`) and never restates it
planning.md reads `nodes chain <path>` only when `nodes` is on PATH, its one optional tie to the nodes pack
